title: Interlock Logic & Cause Effect Matrix - DC-3401A (SEQ-3401)
content:
INTERLOCK LOGIC & CAUSE EFFECT MATRIX: SEQ-3401 (CATALYST REDUCTION REACTOR (DC-3401A) + HEATER EA-3401 LOGIC).
Document No: TJC-LLD-IL-DC-3401A, Revision: Rev.03, Status: Issued for Operation, SIL Level: SIL 2.
Equipment: DC-3401A, Functional Location: TJC-LLD-3400-01.
CAUSE & EFFECT MATRIX (TRIPS):
- T1: Bed temperature HIGH-HIGH (TSHH-3401 > 230 degC, 2oo3) -> Actions: Trip (EFF-1), Close Discharge (EFF-2), Maintain (EFF-4), DCS Alarm (EFF-5)
- T2: Reactor pressure HIGH-HIGH (PSHH-3404 > 5 barg, 1oo2) -> Actions: Trip (EFF-1), Close Discharge (EFF-2), Open Min-Flow (EFF-3), DCS Alarm (EFF-5)
- T3: Outlet O2 HIGH during H2 (inerting fail) (AI-3401 > 100 ppm, 1oo1) -> Actions: Trip (EFF-1), Close Discharge (EFF-2), DCS Alarm (EFF-5)
- T4: Nitrogen carrier flow LOW-LOW (FSLL-17343 < 150 kg/h, 1oo1) -> Actions: Trip (EFF-1), Close Discharge (EFF-2), DCS Alarm (EFF-5)
- T5: Heater element over-temperature (EHT-3401 skin TC > 260 degC, 1oo1) -> Actions: Trip (EFF-1), DCS Alarm (EFF-5)
- T6: Emergency stop (manual) (HS-3401 Manual, 1oo1) -> Actions: Trip (EFF-1), Close Discharge (EFF-2), Open Min-Flow (EFF-3), DCS Alarm (EFF-5)
START PERMISSIVES (AND-gate conditions to start):
- P1: O2 free / inerting done (AI-3401 < 100 ppm) (AI-3401, Gate: AND)
- P2: N2 carrier flow established (> 150 kg/h) (FT-17343, Gate: AND)
- P3: Bed homogeneous 120 degC (all TE within 15 degC) (TE-3401, Gate: AND)
- P4: No active trip / reset done (DCS reset, Gate: AND)
- —: ALL permissives TRUE → START DC-3401A ENABLED (—, Gate: AND)
CROSS REFERENCES: P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-3401, Datasheet: TJC-LLD-DS-DC-3401A.

title: One Point Lesson - Reduction DC-3401A 4-Step Overview (OPL-DC-3401A-01)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-DC-3401A-01 - Reduction DC-3401A 4-Step Overview.

Equipment: DC-3401A, Discipline: Process / Operations, Area: 3400 - CATALYST REDUCTION SYSTEM.

References: Interlock: SEQ-3401 (SIL 2), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-3401.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains reduction dc-3401a 4-step overview for DC-3401A (CATALYST REDUCTION REACTOR) in the CATALYST REDUCTION SYSTEM. The PdO catalyst is shipped in an oxidised state; it must be reduced to Pd before it is active for the process.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Obtain the correct operating permit and brief the shift team before the task.
- Precaution 2: Confirm hazardous fluids are isolated / inerted as required by procedure.
- Precaution 3: Beware of flammable, hot, or high-pressure fluids; wear the correct PPE.
- Precaution 4: Never defeat a safety interlock or trip without an authorised override permit.
- Precaution 5: Have emergency actions and communications ready before starting.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: Operating procedure & P&ID
- Tool 2: Radio / communication with panel
- Tool 3: Gas detector (O2 / LEL) as required
- Tool 4: Correct PPE for the fluid handled
- Tool 5: Sample containers & PPE for sampling
- Tool 6: Permit-to-work documentation

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: 1. Inerting to below 100 ppm O2.
- Step 1 - Check: Permit valid & briefed
- Step 2 - Action: 2. Heating-up bed to 120-135 degC.
- Step 2 - Check: Parameter within limit
- Step 3 - Action: 3. Hydrogen reduction (managing the exotherm).
- Step 3 - Check: Interlock status confirmed
- Step 4 - Action: 4. Cooling down to 30 degC and keeping inert.
- Step 4 - Check: Change logged on DCS
- Step 5 - Action: Handover to next shift.
- Step 5 - Check: Handover to next shift

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: Bed multipoint TC point 3 reading open circuit | Cause: Thermocouple element failed at the sheath junction | Action: Replaced TC point 3 in the multipoint assembly, verified reading.
- Symptom: One heater bank drawing no current, slow heat-up | Cause: Electric heater element bank open circuit / element burnt | Action: Replaced heater element bank, meggered, verified TIC-17343 response
- Symptom: Inerting O2 analyzer drift vs portable reference | Cause: Analyzer zero drift and sample dryer saturated | Action: Recalibrated AI-3401 on span gas, replaced sample dryer

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: The PdO catalyst is shipped in an oxidised state; it must be reduced to Pd before it is active for the process.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-3401: e.g. TSHH-3401 trips at > 230 degC - never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-3401 before working on DC-3401A.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.

References: Interlock: SEQ-3401 (SIL 2), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-3401.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains heating-up & bed homogenisation for DC-3401A (CATALYST REDUCTION REACTOR) in the CATALYST REDUCTION SYSTEM. The catalyst bed must be homogeneous at 120-135 degC before hydrogen is introduced, otherwise the reduction is uneven and can run away locally.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:

- Precaution 2: Confirm hazardous fluids are isolated / inerted as required by procedure.
- Precaution 3: Beware of flammable, hot, or high-pressure fluids; wear the correct PPE.

- Tool 5: Sample containers & PPE for sampling

- Step 1 - Action: Energise heater EA-3401 (power on) after inerting is confirmed
- Step 1 - Check: Permit valid & briefed
- Step 2 - Action: Set the nitrogen carrier flow to about 275 kg/h
- Step 2 - Check: Parameter within limit

title: One Point Lesson - Hydrogen Reduction Safety & Exotherm Control (OPL-DC-3401A-04)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-DC-3401A-04 - Hydrogen Reduction Safety & Exotherm Control.

Equipment: DC-3401A, Discipline: Process / Operations, Area: 3400 - CATALYST REDUCTION SYSTEM.

References: Interlock: SEQ-3401 (SIL 2), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-3401.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains hydrogen reduction safety & exotherm control for DC-3401A in the CATALYST REDUCTION SYSTEM. Hydrogen is flammable over 4-75 % in air. During reduction the PdO->Pd reaction is exothermic and the bed temperature must be watched closely.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Obtain the correct operating permit and brief the shift team before the task.
- Precaution 2: Confirm hazardous fluids are isolated / inerted as required by procedure.
- Precaution 3: Beware of flammable, hot, or high-pressure fluids; wear the correct PPE.
- Precaution 4: Never defeat a safety interlock or trip without an authorised override permit.
- Precaution 5: Have emergency actions and communications ready before starting.

- Tool 4: Correct PPE for the fluid handled
- Tool 5: Sample containers & PPE for sampling
- Tool 6: Permit-to-work documentation

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Introduce H2 only after inerting and bed homogeneity are confirmed
- Step 1 - Check: Permit valid & briefed
- Step 2 - Action: Hold a constant N2+H2 flow for about 12 hours
- Step 2 - Check: Parameter within limit
- Step 3 - Action: Watch TE-3401 for any exotherm approaching the TSHH-3401 limit
- Step 3 - Check: Interlock status confirmed
- Step 4 - Action: If bed exceeds 230 degC the logic auto-trips heater and blocks H2
- Step 4 - Check: Change logged on DCS
- Step 5 - Action: Keep the reactor vent path (PV-3404) available at all times
- Step 5 - Check: Handover to next shift

- Symptom: Inerting O2 analyzer drift vs portable reference | Cause: Analyzer zero drift and sample dryer saturated | Action: Recalibrated AI-3401 on span gas, replaced sample dryer

title: One Point Lesson - Cooling-Down & Catalyst Preservation (OPL-DC-3401A-05)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-DC-3401A-05 - Cooling-Down & Catalyst Preservation.

Equipment: DC-3401A, Discipline: Process / Operations, Area: 3400 - CATALYST REDUCTION SYSTEM.

References: Interlock: SEQ-3401 (SIL 2), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-3401.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains cooling-down & catalyst preservation for DC-3401A in the CATALYST REDUCTION SYSTEM. After reduction the catalyst is pyrophoric; it must be cooled slowly and kept under a nitrogen blanket to prevent re-oxidation or fire.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Obtain the correct operating permit and brief the shift team before the task.
- Precaution 2: Confirm hazardous fluids are isolated / inerted as required by procedure.
- Precaution 3: Beware of flammable, hot, or high-pressure fluids; wear the correct PPE.

- Tool 4: Correct PPE for the fluid handled
- Tool 5: Sample containers & PPE for sampling
- Tool 6: Permit-to-work documentation

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Decrease TIC-17343 slowly, no faster than 0.5 degC/s
- Step 1 - Check: Permit valid & briefed
- Step 2 - Action: Cool all bed thermocouples below 29 degC (ambient)
- Step 2 - Check: Parameter within limit
- Step 3 - Action: Switch off heater EA-3401 (power off) once cool
- Step 3 - Check: Interlock status confirmed
- Step 4 - Action: Isolate the reactor and hold nitrogen pressure at 2 kg/cm2
- Step 4 - Check: Change logged on DCS
- Step 5 - Action: Never open the reactor to air while the catalyst is active
- Step 5 - Check: Handover to next shift

- Symptom: Inerting O2 analyzer drift vs portable reference | Cause: Analyzer zero drift and sample dryer saturated | Action: Recalibrated AI-3401 on span gas, replaced sample dryer

- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-3401: e.g. TSHH-3401 trips at > 230 degC - never defeat it without a permit.

title: One Point Lesson - Multipoint Thermocouple TE-3401 Verification (OPL-DC-3401A-06)
content:

Equipment: DC-3401A, Discipline: Instrument, Area: 3400 - CATALYST REDUCTION SYSTEM.

References: Interlock: SEQ-3401 (SIL 2), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-3401.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains multipoint thermocouple te-3401 verification for DC-3401A in the CATALYST REDUCTION SYSTEM. The 8-point bed temperature profile drives the whole reduction; a failed or drifting thermocouple can hide a hot spot.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: De-energise and isolate the loop; place the function to bypass/inhibit under permit.
- Precaution 2: Inform the panel operator before working on any trip, valve or transmitter.
- Precaution 3: Take care with instrument air / hydraulic pressure when disconnecting tubing.
- Precaution 4: Verify intrinsic-safety / Ex integrity is restored before returning to service.
- Precaution 5: Wear correct PPE and follow ESD/override control procedures.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: HART communicator / positioner software (e.g. ValveLink)
- Tool 2: Loop calibrator & decade box / pressure source
- Tool 3: Digital multimeter and clamp meter
- Tool 4: Span/zero test gas or reference standards
- Tool 5: Torque screwdriver and small hand tools
- Tool 6: Certified test/inhibit permit

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Verify all 8 TE-3401 points are reading and note the spread
- Step 1 - Check: Loop isolated / under permit
- Step 2 - Action: Flag any single TC more than 15 degC off its neighbours
- Step 2 - Check: Reference standard traceable
- Step 3 - Action: Cross-check the profile against TIC-17343 heater outlet
- Step 3 - Check: As-found & as-left recorded
- Step 4 - Action: Replace any open-circuit or drifting TC at the next opportunity
- Step 4 - Check: Trip / control action verified
- Step 5 - Action: Confirm TSHH-3401 selects the highest bed temperature for the trip
- Step 5 - Check: Return to service confirmed

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: Bed multipoint TC point 3 reading open circuit | Cause: Thermocouple element failed at the sheath junction | Action: Replaced TC point 3 in the multipoint assembly, verified reading.
- Symptom: Inerting O2 analyzer drift vs portable reference | Cause: Analyzer zero drift and sample dryer saturated | Action: Recalibrated AI-3401 on span gas, replaced sample dryer
- Symptom: N2 inert valve slow / sticking during inerting step | Cause: Actuator seals hardened, positioner out of calibration | Action: Serviced actuator, replaced seals, recalibrated positioner

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: The 8-point bed temperature profile drives the whole reduction; a failed or drifting thermocouple can hide a hot spot.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-3401: e.g. TSHH-3401 trips at > 230 degC - never defeat it without a permit.

title: One Point Lesson - Manway Gasket & Box-Up After Catalyst Change (OPL-DC-3401A-07)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-DC-3401A-07 - Manway Gasket & Box-Up After Catalyst Change.

Equipment: DC-3401A, Discipline: Mechanical, Area: 3400 - CATALYST REDUCTION SYSTEM.

References: Interlock: SEQ-3401 (SIL 2), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-3401.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains manway gasket & box-up after catalyst change for DC-3401A in the CATALYST REDUCTION SYSTEM. A leaking manway loses inert gas and risks air ingress that could ignite the fresh, active catalyst.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Apply LOTO (Lock-Out Tag-Out) and prove zero energy before starting work.
- Precaution 2: Isolate, depressurise, drain and purge the equipment; obtain a valid work permit.
- Precaution 3: Wear the correct PPE: coverall, safety shoes, gloves, goggles and hearing protection.
- Precaution 4: Beware of stored mechanical energy (springs, rotating inertia) and pinch points.
- Precaution 5: Use certified lifting gear and correct manual-handling technique for heavy parts.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: Standard mechanical hand tools & calibrated torque wrench
- Tool 2: LOTO padlocks and permit
- Tool 3: Laser/dial alignment kit (as applicable)
- Tool 4: Feeler gauges, dial indicator, seal/bearing pullers
- Tool 5: Correct spare parts and gaskets per the BOM
- Tool 6: Lifting gear and slings (certified)

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Always fit a new spiral-wound SS316/graphite gasket
- Step 1 - Check: Isolation & LOTO verified
- Step 2 - Action: Torque the manway bolts in a star pattern to the specified value
- Step 2 - Check: Parts match BOM / spec
- Step 3 - Action: Leak test the joint with nitrogen at 2 kg/cm2
- Step 3 - Check: Torque / clearance to spec
- Step 4 - Action: Record the catalyst batch number and the loaded volume (3.2 m3)
- Step 4 - Check: No leak / smooth operation
- Step 5 - Action: Re-instate PSV-3401 and all instruments before start-up
- Step 5 - Check: Record in equipment history

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: Scheduled statutory PSV pop test | Cause: Set pressure drift +0.3 barg found | Action: Overhauled PSV-3401, lapped seat, re-set to 6 barg, certified
- Symptom: End-of-life catalyst replacement at turnaround | Cause: Spent Pd/Al2O3 catalyst at end of run | Action: Vacuumed out spent catalyst, inspected grids, loaded 3.2 m3 fresh cat.
- Symptom: Nitrogen leak at bottom manway during leak test | Cause: Spiral-wound gasket unevenly seated | Action: Renewed SW SS316/graphite gasket, re-torqued in star pattern, leak tested.

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: A leaking manway loses inert gas and risks air ingress that could ignite the fresh, active catalyst.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-3401: e.g. TSHH-3401 trips at > 230 degC - never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-3401 before working on DC-3401A.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.

title: Piping & Instrumentation Diagram Register - DC-3401A
content:
PIPING & INSTRUMENTATION DIAGRAM (P&ID) REGISTER: DC-3401A (CATALYST REDUCTION REACTOR).
Document No: TJC-LLD-PID-3401, Revision: N/A, Status: Issued for Operation.
Area: 3400 – Catalyst Preparation, Functional Location: TJC-LLD-3400-01.
INSTRUMENT & PROCESS CONTROL LOOPS:
- TSHH-3401: Bed temperature HIGH-HIGH (Temperature Switch) [Setpoint: > 230 degC]. Function: Trip initiator T1 → SEQ-3401. Location: Reactor bed
- TE-3401: Multipoint Thermocouple (8 points) (Temperature Element). Function: Bed temperature profile monitoring. Location: Reactor bed
- PSHH-3404: Reactor pressure HIGH-HIGH (Pressure Switch) [Setpoint: > 5 barg]. Function: Trip initiator T2 → SEQ-3401. Location: Reactor vent line
- PI-3404: Reactor Pressure Indicator (Pressure Indicator). Function: Local pressure indication. Location: Reactor vent line
- AI-3401: Outlet O2 Analyzer (Analyzer) [Setpoint: > 100 ppm]. Function: Trip initiator T3 & Permissive P1. Location: Reactor outlet line
